title: Architecture Decision Record frontmatter
description: Frontmatter for an ADR under docs/decisions/. Carries the ADR status vocabulary and the two conditional obligations the standard places on it: an accepted record owes its decision makers and what it governs, and a superseded record owes the identifier of the record that replaced it.

id.description: Stable document identifier. It does not change when the title or filename does.

type.description: Document category, from the standard's closed set.

status.description: Lifecycle state, from this type's controlled vocabulary. Agents do not invent statuses.

updated.description: Optional. Git already knows when the file changed; set this only where the document's own sense of currency differs from its last commit.

reviewed.description: Date a person or agent deliberately checked the document against reality and found it still true. Set it only where a review cadence has been declared.

owners.description: Who is answerable for the content. The first entry is the one answerable.

related.description: Declared relationships. Optional, so an absent relation proves nothing.

depends_on.description: Documents this one depends on. A separate field from `related`, not a relation within it.

supersedes.description: The record this one replaces. Reciprocated by that record's `superseded_by`.

superseded_by.description: The record that replaced this one. Reciprocated by that record's `supersedes`.

url.description: Canonical location, for a document that gets copied out of the repository.

discussion.description: Where the argument happened: the pull request, issue or thread. Carried on the types that are argued before they are settled.

decision_makers.description: Who decided. Required and non-empty at `accepted`, because an ADR that does not record who decided cannot answer whether the right person did. A `proposed` record legitimately carries an empty list: nobody has decided yet.

informed.description: Optional. Who was told about the outcome.

governs.description: What this decision binds. An item is a repository name when the record binds a whole repository, which is the usual case in this tree, or a target when it binds one document. Both forms may appear in one list. Required at `accepted` and may be empty: an empty list means considered and there is none, while an absent field claims the question does not apply.

identifier.description: A document identifier such as SPEC-0012, ADR-0017 or ARCH-SECURITY.

target.description: A reference resolvable from outside this document: an identifier (SPEC-0004), a qualified identifier (lexicon:SPEC-0004), an issue or pull request (argus#142), or a repository-relative path to a document that has no identifier (docs/plans/2026-09-11-project-doc-template.md). A path target is never qualified with a repository prefix.

relatedEntry.description: One declared relationship, as a predicate and what it points at.

repository.description: A repository name, such as lexicon or projects.

governed.description: What a decision binds: a repository name, or a target naming one document.

allOf.$comment: An accepted decision owes its decision makers, named rather than merely listed, and what it governs.
A superseded decision owes the identifier that replaced it. The reciprocal check, that the named record points back, spans two documents and belongs to the validator rather than to any schema.

$comment: The standard states one transition for this type, supersession, and records it as an append rather than an edit. No full transition table is stated, so none is carried here.
